testArchitectureAssessment.controllerUnit: A small explicitly synthetic solver fixture may test asynchronous pause/resume, stale delivery rejection, one publication and terminal cleanup cheaply while retaining the real solver and accepted physics metrics. Alternatively an injected deterministic worker tests controller behavior, but requires a larger production seam. Do not manufacture a native-product claim from synthetic data.
testArchitectureAssessment.nativeIntegration: Keep actual Clavellium scene pause test and actual native solver/accepted settled frame coverage. Do not remove or replace the native test solely because a synthetic controller test passes.
testArchitectureAssessment.preferredMinimalRepairAfterProof: If native solver completes accepted within measured larger budget and optimized unchanged test succeeds, a documented numerical integration wait allowance is proportionate. Existing30second native timeout is a wall-clock assumption, distinct from every physical assertion. Moving or splitting controller tests is optional test architecture work, not necessary proof of source fix.
testArchitectureAssessment.fixturePreparation: Raw controller fixture differs from scene accepted prepareDisplay seed. Preparing accepted seed can improve fixture consistency, but current raw steps remain geometry accepted; this change alone cannot explain or fix cost of waiting0.5simseconds.
